target: F1's hard acceptance at fixture revision 4: the sixteen predicates that decide CAD_PASS, the two that decide 3MF_PASS, and the structural guards -- the request leak audit, the reference digest, the registration datum and the distance mask
note:
Run with: uv run python tools/mutate.py benchmarks/mutations/e2e-f1-gridbin.json

TWO KINDS OF MUTATION, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. Rows against tools/f1_candidate.py mutate the CANDIDATE: they build a defective bin and prove the predicate notices the defect, which is what the brief's section 6/F1 'required mutation probes' asks for. Rows against tools/e2e.py mutate the INSTRUMENT: they weaken a gate and prove a test notices the gate weakening. A fixture with only the second kind proves its tests read its own code; a fixture with only the first proves nothing about the gates the candidate never trips.

The brief requires seven probes. Six are here as candidate mutations -- divider removed, divider on the wrong axis, lip removed, magnet holes added, one axis scaled, an extra body in the STL (and again in the 3MF). The seventh, a mirrored or wrong-handed transform, is qualified in the brief itself: 'IF the fixture gains any handed feature'. This one has not, and that is measured rather than assumed -- the mirrored reference registers back onto the original at p99 = 4.4e-11 mm through a proper rotation (benchmarks/e2e/f1-gridbin.json, calibration.measurements.mirror_p99_mm). So the probe that stands in its place is the property that would matter if the fixture ever did gain one: that the registration cannot fit a reflection at all. It is exercised against a deliberately handed solid, because a reflection guard tested on an achiral part passes whether or not it exists.

REVISION 2 ADDED SIX HARD PREDICATES AND TWO STRUCTURAL CHANGES, AND SECTION 12 OF THE BRIEF SAYS WHAT THAT COSTS: 'Every predicate that can cause PASS/FAIL must have a mutation that proves it can fail.' Each of the six has one below, and two of them reproduce the exact deviations the first real run produced -- a 2.4 mm capture ramp against a published 2.15, and a 4.0 mm corner radius against a published 3.75 -- so the fixture's claim to be able to see them is a measurement rather than an argument. The registration datum and the distance mask are gates too, and both are mutated: a mask that stops masking, a mask that masks everything, and a datum that goes back to centring bounding boxes.

Every entry below was run against the real code and observed to fail its named test.

mutations.name: divider-removed
mutations.why: probe 1. One divider is two compartments, and the cavity cross-section is where that is visible: two interior rings become one. A bin with no divider has the right footprint, the right base, the right height, the right wall and the right lip, so every other predicate accepts it

mutations.name: divider-on-the-short-axis
mutations.why: probe 2. One divider in the wrong place. Every counting predicate still reads two compartments -- this is the defect that a count alone cannot see, which is why the split axis is measured by the disjointness of the two cavity footprints and not by their number

mutations.name: stack-lip-removed
mutations.why: probe 3. A lip as deep as the wall is no ledge at all, so the next bin up has nothing to land on. The bin's envelope, volume and compartment topology barely move, so a dimensional score would call this correct

mutations.name: the-lip-is-too-shallow
mutations.why: revision 2, and the difference from the row above is the whole reason both exist. A 2.0 mm lip is still a ledge -- `stack_lip_present` accepts it, because it protrudes 1.0 mm past the wall -- and it is 0.6 mm off the published depth, which is the surface the next bin's foot actually seats against. Only a predicate that reads the published figure can refuse it

mutations.name: the-lip-seat-sits-high
mutations.why: revision 2. The lip is the published shape at the published depth and it is 0.4 mm too high, so a stack of ten runs 4 mm long. Chosen at 0.4 rather than something gross on purpose: the overall height stays inside the published band, so `height_mm` still passes and this is the only row that can see it

mutations.name: the-base-plug-runs-the-capture-ramp-long
mutations.why: revision 2, and the exact deviation the first real run produced: a 2.4 mm upper chamfer where the publication says 2.15. Revision 1 could not fault it, because revision 1 did not state the profile -- it failed the surface distance instead, on a surface the request had withheld, which is the whole of the reviewer's ruling. The footprint, height, corner radius, floor, divider and lip rows all still pass

mutations.name: the-bin-stands-on-one-plinth
mutations.why: revision 2. The published base profile is stated per grid unit with the published gap kept between units, so a two-cell bin stands on two feet -- and one plinth of the same outline has the SAME bounding box at every height, so both footprint rows and the profile row accept it while it will not seat on a baseplate. Measured on the reference: two rounded squares at z = 4.75 (area 3420.306 mm2) becoming one outline at z = 5.00 (3453.161)

mutations.name: the-corner-radius-is-four-millimetres
mutations.why: revision 2, and the other deviation the first real run produced. A corner rounder than the socket it drops into jams on the way in, and it costs 0.25 mm on a published 3.75 -- invisible to every span, every count and every band the fixture had at revision 1

mutations.name: the-floor-is-the-top-of-the-plug
mutations.why: revision 2, and the third of the first run's choices. The published base is one height unit including the structure tying the feet together, so a floor at the top of the plug hollows out the base itself -- two millimetres of extra usable depth bought from the part of the bin that does the locating

mutations.name: magnet-pockets-in-the-base
mutations.why: probe 4. The brief forbids magnets and screw holes; both are bores through a base section that is otherwise solid, so an interior ring anywhere in the base band is one or the other

mutations.name: finger-scoops-in-both-compartments
mutations.why: a forbidden feature the brief names alongside the magnets. A scoop is a ramp at the compartment floor, so the open area stops being the same at every height -- which is the same measurement that catches a label flange, and the reason the predicate is stated as 'prismatic' rather than as two feature detectors

mutations.name: label-flange-under-the-rim
mutations.why: the fourth forbidden feature. The tab is drawn deep enough to reach inside the compartment band on purpose: a flange confined to the top of the compartment is outside what this predicate can see, and that limit is recorded in the fixture rather than hidden by a mutation drawn to avoid it

mutations.name: the-long-axis-scaled-five-percent
mutations.why: probe 5. A bin wider than its cells does not drop into the grid. At revision 2 the requirement is the published footprint rather than a range on the undersize, because the request now states the gap the family leaves in a cell

mutations.name: the-short-axis-exactly-one-pitch
mutations.why: the other footprint axis, and the boundary rather than a gross error: a bin exactly as wide as its cell binds. The published gap is 0.5 mm and the stated tolerance is 0.2, so this is refused by 0.3 mm

mutations.name: the-bin-is-a-height-unit-too-tall
mutations.why: the height band at revision 2 is the published body plus somewhere between the lip's published land and the whole published lip -- 23.5 to 25.4 -- so it is narrow enough to be worth mutating, where revision 1's 21 to 28 was not. A bin one height unit tall by mistake is the defect a requester notices when the drawer will not close

mutations.name: an-extra-body-in-the-stl
mutations.why: probe 7, STL half. A stray solid floating above the bin is a second thing on the plate and an STL cannot object -- the format has no notion of a body, so the count comes from connected components

mutations.name: an-extra-body-in-the-3mf-is-not-counted
mutations.why: probe 7, 3MF half. The extra body is hidden as a second COMPONENT of the placed assembly rather than as a second build item, which is where this repository's own writer puts every part. A reader that walks only the first component reports one printable body and the archive ships with two

mutations.name: a-reflection-is-admitted-to-the-pose-set
mutations.why: probe 6, in the only form this fixture can honestly carry it. Brief section 4: a mirrored part must not become a PASS because a fitter found a reflection. The bin is achiral so it cannot detect this; the test uses a right-handed tripod whose three arms have distinct lengths, so a proper rotation cannot map it onto its mirror image and an improper one can

mutations.name: the-registration-centres-bounding-boxes-again
mutations.why: revision 2's datum, which is a gate and not a convenience. The publication cannot fix the overall height, so two correct bins may differ by up to 1.9 mm; a centroid fit turns half of that into a z offset on every surface, including the base plug the request now dimensions exactly. The mutation is the revision-1 behaviour, restored

mutations.name: the-distance-mask-stops-masking-the-lip
mutations.why: the ruling in one line: a surface judged by reference distance must be determined by request-side facts, and the region above the lip's published land is not -- the final chamfer cannot be built in full at a 1.0 mm wall and the publication does not say how far to truncate it. A mask that stops applying there fails a candidate for choosing a legal truncation, which is the defect the whole revision exists to remove

mutations.name: the-distance-mask-stops-masking-the-floor-transition
mutations.why: the other masked range, and the one that is measured rather than argued: with it in place an independent implementation of the published figures scores p99 = 0.0018 mm, and without it 0.300 -- exactly on the band. The publication fixes the floor height and not the fillet that meets it, and the same public file offers 2.8 mm where the reference uses 1.1

mutations.name: the-distance-mask-stops-masking-the-feet-to-body-tie
mutations.why: revision 3, and the half of run 02's finding that the distance row carried. The publication gives the base one height unit INCLUDING the structure tying the feet together and gives the profile 4.75 of it, so the tie happens somewhere in the 2.25 mm between and nothing says where -- measured, the reference spends 0.25 mm of it and run 02's candidate spends all of it, because the body overhangs the feet and the brief forbids supports. Bucketed by height, that span was the whole of run 02's disagreement: p99 1.2280 against 0.0000 in every band above it

mutations.name: the-corner-radius-is-read-inside-the-base
mutations.why: revision 3, and the other half. The mutation is revision 2's own probe height, 6.0 mm, restored. It reads the outline where the feet are still becoming a body, and the area-deficit formula assumes a rounded rectangle -- so what comes back is not a radius: 6.7724 on a part whose radius is 3.7528 at every height it has one. The test measures it on a solid built to have two feet at that height, because a probe height is only wrong against geometry that uses the freedom the publication leaves

mutations.name: the-divider-exclusion-is-removed
mutations.why: revision 4, and run 03's finding. Above the compartment band the request fixes the divider's existence, axis and thickness and stops fixing how far it continues toward the lip -- measured, the reference runs it to 20.95 and run 03's candidate stopped at 18.25, and neither is wrong. Without the exclusion two bins differing in nothing else fail the row at p99 0.3849

mutations.name: the-divider-exclusion-broadens-into-the-whole-height-band
mutations.why: the other half, and the one the reviewer named as deciding whether this is a repair at all. Conditions 1 and 2 are both satisfiable by a mask that quietly swallows everything above the compartments -- which would hide lip and support defects and be the truth-model problem in reverse. The control is a lip support missing along a whole long side, at the same heights the exclusion operates in and outside it in space: it fails the row at p99 0.8097 with the exclusion bounded, and passes with it broadened

mutations.name: a-mask-that-removes-everything-reports-a-clean-distance
mutations.why: the failure mode a mask introduces that a band does not have: a mask wide enough to drop every sample leaves a row that cannot fail, and a row that cannot fail reads exactly like one that holds. The refusal is loud on purpose, and it has to be a refusal rather than a percentile of nothing

mutations.name: the-surface-distance-is-one-way
mutations.why: brief section 4.6. Every point of a plain box has a near neighbour on the same box with a spike on it, so the one-way distance stays at zero however much geometry the candidate added. This is the direction a missing feature hides in

mutations.name: the-distance-row-cannot-fail
mutations.why: the calibrated band is the fixture's only whole-shape gate, and a gate that cannot fail reads exactly like one that holds. Both states are asserted -- matching geometry passes it, mismatching geometry fails it -- because a row pinned only on the failing side can be satisfied by a scorer that always fails

mutations.name: an-open-surface-passes-the-watertight-row
mutations.why: an unclosed candidate has no volume and no defensible moments, and every downstream number computed from it is a divergence sum over a boundary that does not close. The row is one field wide, which is exactly the kind nobody checks

mutations.name: a-missing-3mf-reports-present
mutations.why: the brief requires a 3MF, and a run that produced none must say so rather than reporting an absent gate as clear. Brief section 1.4: never describe a skipped fixture as coverage

mutations.name: the-3mf-unit-is-not-checked
mutations.why: 3MF's default unit is the micron. An unstated or wrong unit is a thousandfold scale error, and the geometry rows would report it as a shape disagreement rather than as the unit problem it is

mutations.name: an-unreadable-archive-raises-instead-of-reporting
mutations.anchor: except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile, E2EError, ValueError) as exc:
mutations.why: a corrupt deliverable is a finding the report has to carry. An exception out of the gate is a run that produces no report at all, which is worse than a failing row because there is nothing to read

mutations.name: the-request-audit-excuses-every-coincidence
mutations.anchor: undeclared = [pair for pair in found if pair[1] not in declared]
mutations.why: the requester-side prohibition, and the one guard whose absence produces a number indistinguishable from a real one. It matters more at revision 2, not less: the request now legitimately states two of the reference's three extents, so the guard is the only thing standing between a declared disclosure and an undeclared one

mutations.name: the-reference-digest-is-not-verified
mutations.why: a drifted reference is worse than a missing one, because a benchmark scored against it produces a number that looks exactly like a real one. The digest is checked on every call and not once at ingest, for the reason tools/corpus.py gives: a hash taken when the file arrived says nothing about the file this run is about to read
